threads.body: `ignoredClassLoaders` is a mutable static that’s read on the class-definition hot path and updated via `setIgnoredClassLoadersPredicate(...)`. As written it isn’t `volatile` (or otherwise safely published), so other threads may keep seeing the old predicate after installation. Also, the setter accepts `null`, which would lead to an NPE later. Consider (1) making the field `volatile` (or using an `AtomicReference`), (2) rejecting `null` (e.g., defaulting to a predicate that always returns false), and (3) reducing the setter visibility to package-private since it’s only used within `io.opentelemetry.javaagent.tooling` (per minimal-visibility guidance).

`beforeDefineClass(...)` passes `classLoader` directly into `ignoredClassLoaders.test(...)`, but `classLoader` can be `null` for bootstrap-loaded classes. Today the predicate set from `AgentInstaller` handles null, but since `setIgnoredClassLoadersPredicate(...)` is public and doesn’t document/enforce null handling, this is easy to misuse and would cause an NPE on the class-definition path. Consider guarding here (`classLoader != null && ...`) and/or enforcing a non-null, null-tolerant predicate in the setter.
